explanation: Claude Joseph Rouget de Lisle wrote it as a war song for the Army of the Rhine. It took its name from volunteers from Marseille, who sang it as they marched into Paris.

claims.text: 'La Marseillaise' was written in Strasbourg in April 1792 by Claude Joseph Rouget de Lisle.
'La Marseillaise' was not written in Marseille, Paris or Lyon.
Rouget de Lisle wrote the song for the French Army of the Rhine, under the title 'Chant de guerre pour l'Armée du Rhin'.
The song was named after volunteers from Marseille who sang it as they marched into Paris in 1792.
